substitutions.pattern:
**Defaults for every `Task` call.** `run_in_background: true`, agent mode (readonly strips MCP), file pointers not inlined context, and an explicit model per role, Project workers included. `/setup-pstack` writes `~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc`, whose per-role lines override the defaults below and the role models in the routed skills (`arena`, `swarm`, `interrogate`). A role with no line keeps its default. A line of `inherit-parent` or `auto` runs the role on the parent model, so omit `model` and spawn `generalPurpose`, because `poteto-agent` defaults to Opus 5.5. Each code playbook reads its own line (`feature, refactoring`, `bug-fix`, `perf-issue`, or `hillclimb`), prose and judgment read `judgment and prose`, and trivial mechanical edits read `swarm workers`. If the rule has no `# defaults: 3` line, an older setup wrote it. Keep honoring its lines, and tell the user once per session to rerun `/setup-pstack`.

- Code, prose, and judgment: `claude-opus-5-5-xhigh-fast`.
- Trivial mechanical edits: `claude-opus-5-5-high-fast`.
- Diverse review and design panels: one runner each on `claude-fable-5-2-high`, `claude-opus-5-5-high-fast`, and `gemini-4-neon-xhigh`.

**Fable 5.2 is an exception.** It runs outside a panel only when the user named it for this task or two Opus 5.5 xhigh runs of the same brief failed its check. Say which. Difficulty alone never qualifies.

**Match the model to the job.** Start from the role's line or default, keep its family, and set the level the job needs. The `/setup-pstack` budget sets each role's starting level. Panel seats keep their listed level. Raise any other role one step, up to xhigh, for the hardest or subtlest work, lower it one step for judgment, and two or more steps for routine work. No role runs above xhigh. Opus 5.5 always runs its `-fast` slug. Verification always runs on the `swarm workers` model, `claude-opus-5-5-high-fast` by default. A Gemini seat runs at `gemini-4-neon-xhigh` unless its line names another level. If the Task tool rejects a slug, never pass it again. Fall back to the role's line or default, then the calling skill's fallback, then the closest valid slug of the same family, then omit `model`. Say so.
substitutions.replacement: **Defaults for delegation.** Pass file pointers to each agent. Resolve each role with the Codex router and pass the returned `model` and `reasoning_effort` unchanged. Use the role named by the playbook for implementation, `judgment and prose` for judgment and prose, and `swarm workers` for verification and trivial edits. Resolve each panel slot in order.
substitutions.rationale: Codex resolves model and effort pairs through its role sheet and catalog

substitutions.pattern: 3. Pick the runners from the `arena runners` line in `~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc`, by default `claude-fable-5-2-high`, `claude-opus-5-5-high-fast`, and `gemini-4-neon-xhigh`. An `auto` or `inherit-parent` entry is the parent model, so omit `model` and spawn `generalPurpose`. If the Task tool rejects a slug, use the nearest valid slug of the same family or drop the seat, keep at least two runners, and say so. Families go by prefix, and the longest match wins: `claude-fable-*`, `claude-*`, and `gemini-*`, after dropping a leading `cursor-`. Any other slug's family is its text before the first hyphen. Spawn more for multiple design directions, and repeat one model when the work is generation-bound, not judgment-sensitive. Pick each subagent's reasoning level per the Subagents section of the **poteto-mode** skill.
substitutions.replacement: 3. Resolve `arena runners` through [Codex routing](../poteto-mode/references/codex-routing.md) and use the returned `spawn` payloads in order. Configure more slots to compare more design directions. Repeat a model when the work needs more candidates.
substitutions.rationale: Codex gets Arena runner defaults from its routing catalog

substitutions.pattern: After all Phase B candidates complete, spawn one readonly judge from the `arena cross-judge pool` line in `~/.cursor/rules/pstack-models.mdc`, by default `claude-opus-5-5-high-fast`, `gemini-4-neon-xhigh`. The judge is never from the parent's vendor, and Fable counts as Claude for that check, so use the first entry from another vendor. An `auto` or `inherit-parent` entry is the parent model. If you do not know the parent's model, use the first real slug and say that the vendor check did not run. If the Task tool rejects a slug, use the nearest valid slug of the same family, then the next such entry, or skip the judge, and say so. While you read in Phase D, the judge scores each candidate, by path label, on each rubric criterion and recommends a base.
substitutions.replacement: After all Phase B candidates complete, choose one read-only judge. Resolve `arena cross-judge pool` in order through [Codex routing](../poteto-mode/references/codex-routing.md). For a pool with multiple entries, pass the candidate's zero-based index as `choice`. Use the first supported resolved model whose provider differs from the parent's provider. Fable and Opus both count as Anthropic. If the parent's model is unknown, use the first supported entry and say you could not check the provider. If no candidate qualifies, say so and continue to Phase D. While you read in Phase D, the judge scores each candidate, by path label, on each rubric criterion and recommends a base.
substitutions.rationale: Codex resolves one eligible Arena judge from its configured pool
